We cannot assure you that we will be able to maintain historic levels of business and/or negotiate and execute long term contracts on terms that are commercially viable with our significant customers or that we will be able to significantly reduce customer concentration in the future.

Negative cash flows from investing activities were mainly due to investments in plant and machinery, processing facilities, and other capital expenditures undertaken in the ordinary course of business.

Our working capital requirements are influenced by factors such as inventory levels maintained prior to the sowing season, credit terms extended to customers, timing of collections, and payment terms with suppliers.
Any delay in collection of receivables, higher-than-anticipated inventory build-up, or reduction in customary supplier credit terms may result in increased working capital requirements.
Our Company’s manufacturing operations are subject to variability in capacity utilisation, which may adversely affect our business, results of operations, and financial condition.
As on March 31, 2026, our installed processing capacity was 9,800 MTPA, against which actual production stood at 5,465 MTPA, reflecting a utilisation of 55.77% for the period.
For the financial year ended March 31, 2025, our installed capacity was 8,400 MTPA, with actual production of 3,192 MTPA, resulting in capacity utilisation of 38.00%.
In comparison, capacity utilisation for the financial years ended March 31, 2024 was 68.75%.
The installed capacity of our processing facilities varies depending on the type and variant of seeds being processed, grading requirements, and operational configurations.

Further, our production volumes and capacity utilisation are influenced by several factors, including availability of raw seeds, seasonal and climatic conditions, agricultural output, farmer participation, demand fluctuations, product mix, regulatory requirements, and logistical constraints.

Any adverse climatic conditions, changes in sowing patterns, lower crop yields, or shifts in farmer preferences may result in lower availability of raw materials and reduced demand for our products, which could lead to under-utilisation of our installed capacity.
Prolonged periods of low capacity utilisation may result in higher per-unit operating costs, reduced operating leverage, and may adversely impact our profitability and cash flows.

Any inability to adequately protect or enforce our trademark rights, or any adverse outcome of disputes relating to our intellectual property, may have an adverse effect on our business, reputation, goodwill, and results of operations.
